_comment: Boundary conditions measured from the existing STAR-CCM+ dataset (Case_07 low fan, Case_16 high fan). These are held FIXED across every generated case so that FCU LAYOUT is the only variable. Extracted with the patch-level A5 rule (cluster, then label by the sign of MEAN w) -- the per-point sign rule misclassifies return fringes as supply and reports 6 supply panels instead of 3.

room.note: walls x=0/8.8, y=0/6.1, floor z=0, ceiling z=3.2; vents recessed at z=3.35 in a plenum above the ceiling

supply.bc_type: fixedValue - the CFD value is EXACTLY constant on every point

return.bc_type: pressure outlet - w VARIES per panel (0.316/0.351/0.372), so it is a result, not a prescribed value

leak.bc_type: pressure outlet - the flow through it is a RESULT, not prescribed
leak._comment: CORRECTED 2026-09-03. The earlier entry claimed ~0.232 m3/s from a supply-minus-return imbalance and asserted the case would not converge without it. That is wrong by 258x: Leak.csv in Case_05 has a mean surface speed of 0.0678 m/s over 0.01331 m2, i.e. 0.0009 m3/s, and the fluid in the door undercut moves at -0.0004 m/s. Prescribing 0.232 m3/s forces 15.5 m/s through the slot and drove a room-wide draft toward the door: whole-room mean speed came out 1.20 m/s against the reference 0.197, almost all of it a coherent v = -0.82. The leak is a pressure outlet that carries almost nothing.
leak._unresolved: The vents in Case_05 do not balance either: net flux over the six panels is -0.192 m3/s (net inflow) while the leak removes 0.0009. So the CSV-sampled vent fluxes are not mass-consistent -- most likely the return panels are point-sampled with a bias, since supply w is exactly constant and return w varies. Do not build a BC on the imbalance.

thermal_bcs_UNKNOWN._comment: No surface CSV carries temperature, so the original wall/furniture thermal BCs are not recoverable from the data. We CHOOSE a set and hold it fixed across all our cases; this makes our dataset internally consistent even though it will not reproduce the STAR-CCM+ cases exactly. Values below are the near-surface fluid temperature measured within 5 cm of each surface in Case_07, used as fixed-value wall temperatures.

reference._comment: The CFD pressure is reduced against rho0 ~ 0.997, NOT the 1.204 rho_ref in the stats file (inherited finding). Any buoyancy term must use 0.997.
